sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Checking Python and creating the environment
sections.what: Checks that python3 is installed, creates the private venv folder if it is missing, activates it, and upgrades pip. Users see numbered step messages.
sections.why: Likely reason: a private environment keeps this project's libraries separate from other projects on the machine.
sections.watch_out: The script checks that python3 exists but not that it is version 3.10 or newer, so an old Python can fail later during installation.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Installing libraries and creating settings
sections.what: Installs everything in requirements.txt and stops with a message if that fails. Copies .env.example to .env if .env is missing, then prints next steps.
sections.why: Likely reason: installing the libraries is required before the app can start, and the settings file gives the user a place for the key.
sections.watch_out: The script does not check that the API key was filled in, so the app will only report the missing key when it starts.

summary: A one-time setup script that creates the app's private Python environment, installs the libraries and creates the settings file.
purpose: Gets a new computer ready to run the app.
why: Its messages and numbered steps are written for a first-time user. Likely reason: a separate environment keeps this project's libraries apart from other Python work.
how: Checks that python3 exists, creates the venv folder if missing, activates it, upgrades pip, installs everything in requirements.txt, copies .env.example to .env if .env is missing, and prints next steps.
inputs: python3 on the machine; requirements.txt; an optional .env.example.
outputs: A venv folder with the libraries installed, and a .env file to fill in.
risks: Does not check the Python version even though 3.10 is required. Does not check that the API key was filled in. Stops on install failure but not on a pip upgrade failure.
debug: Read the step number where it stopped. If the install fails, check the messages above the error. If the app later says the key is missing, open .env and add it. Re-running is safe because existing venv and .env are kept.
